data.name: Ahdaaf
data.gender_notes: Ahdaaf is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Those who protect and defend. The name Ahdaaf carries the meaning “Defenders” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ahdaaf usually hope their child will grow to embody defenders and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a strong and courageous girl, who will be a defender and protector of her loved ones
data.etymology: Ahdaaf belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Defenders.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ahdaaf total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: أهداف
in_arabic.meaning: الأهداف هي الغايات أو النتائج المرغوبة التي يسعى لتحقيقها الشخص
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أهداف مشتق من الهدف، ويعني الغاية أو النتيجة المرغوبة. في اللغة العربية، الهدف هو الشيء الذي يُرمى إليه أو يُسعى لتحقيقه. في السياق الإسلامي، يمكن أن تشير الأهداف إلى الأهداف الروحية أو الدينية التي يسعى المسلمون لتحقيقها في حياتهم، مثل تحقيق الإيمان الصادق، أو العمل الصالح، أو طلب رضا الله تعالى.

in_urdu.name: اہداف
in_urdu.meaning: اہداف وہ مقاصد یا مطلوبہ نتائج ہیں جن کی طرف شخص مائل ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: اسم اہداف کا مطلب ہے مقصد یا مطلوبہ نتیجہ۔ یہ نام عربی زبان کے 'ہدف' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے مقصد یا نشانہ۔ اسلامی تقالید میں، اہداف (أهداف) کو روحانی یا دینی مقاصد کے طور پر سمجھا جا سکتا ہے جن کو مسلمان اپنی زندگی میں حاصل کرنے کی کوشش کرتے ہیں، جیسے کہ صادقانہ عقیدہ، نیک اعمال، یا اللہ کی رضا حاصل کرنا۔

in_hindi.name: अहदाफ
in_hindi.meaning: अहदाफ वे उद्देश्य या वांछित परिणाम हैं जिनकी ओर व्यक्ति प्रवृत्त होता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: अहदाफ नाम का अर्थ है उद्देश्य या वांछित परिणाम। यह नाम अरबी भाषा के 'हदफ' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है उद्देश्य या लक्ष्य। इस्लामी परंपरा में, अहदाफ (أهداف) को आध्यात्मिक या धार्मिक उद्देश्यों के रूप में समझा जा सकता है जिन्हें मुसलमान अपनी जीवन में प्राप्त करने का प्रयास करते हैं, जैसे कि सच्चा विश्वास, अच्छे कर्म, या अल्लाह की कृपा प्राप्त करना।

in_pashto.name: اهداف
in_pashto.meaning: اهداف هغه موخې يا غوښتل شوي پايلې دي کومې چې د يو چا په لور روان دي
in_pashto.long_meaning: د اهدافو نوم مانا يې موخې يا غوښتل شوي پايلې دي. دا نوم د عربي ژبې د 'هدف' څخه اخيستل شوی دی، کوم چې د موخې يا نښانې معنی لري. په اسلامي دود کې، اهداف (أهداف) کولاى شي روحاني يا دينی موخې وښايي کومې چې مسلمانان د خپلو ژوندونو په اوږدو کې د ترلاسه کولو هڅه کوي، لکه د رښتينو ایمان، نیک کارونه، يا د الله رضا ترلاسه کول.

in_english.name: Ahdaaf
in_english.meaning: Ahdaaf refers to goals, objectives, or desired outcomes one strives for
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ahdaaf is derived from the Arabic root 'h-d-f', meaning goal, target, or objective. In Islamic tradition, Ahdaaf (أهداف) can signify spiritual or religious objectives that Muslims strive to achieve in their lives, such as attaining sincere faith, performing righteous deeds, or seeking Allah's pleasure. The name implies a sense of direction, purpose, and aspiration towards betterment and spiritual growth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ahdaaf" is an Arabic term that refers to individuals or groups who protect and defend, particularly in the context of sports or other communal organizations. The cultural significance of this name is rooted in Islamic values of unity, cooperation, and community service. The concept of protecting and defending is a common theme in Islamic teachings, particularly in regards to the protection of theProphet Muhammad (pbuh) and the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Ahdaaf" can be seen as a reflection of the role of believers in guarding their faith and propagating Islamic values in their communities. The term can be understood as a call to action for Muslims to be vigilant in defending the truth and preserving the purity of their religion, as well as in protecting the rights and dignity of their fellow human beings. This spiritual significance is reinforced in the Hadith, which states that "whosejourney is for the sake of Allah and whose final destination is Allah, Allah will make him enter through every gate of Paradise" (Sahih Bukhari). By embracing the role of protector and defender, the believer fulfills this divine obligation and ensures that they are on the path to spiritual growth and eternal reward.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ahdaaf refers to the sacred objectives or goals that draw believers closer to Allah. In Islamic teachings, these objectives include seeking knowledge, performing good deeds, and observing religious practices. The name symbolizes the journey towards spiritual growth and the pursuit of a deeper connection with the Divine.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The term 'Ahdaaf' is mentioned in the hadiths attributed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), referring to the retreats or training camps for Sahabah (companions of the Prophet) to prepare for military expeditions and study Islamic knowledge under the guidance of their leaders. This practice was common during the early Islamic period, particularly during the caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (634-644 AD).
historical_references.time_period: Early Islamic period, Caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (634-644 AD)

historical_references.reference: The term 'Ahdaaf' is also used in the works of classical Islamic scholars such as Ibn Taymiyah (1263-1328 AD) and Ibn Qayyim Al-Jawziyah (1292-1350 AD), who wrote extensively on the importance of 'Ahdaaf' as places of study and spiritual retreat for students and scholars of Islam. These scholars emphasized the role of 'Ahdaaf' in preserving the Islamic tradition and transmitting knowledge from one generation to the next.
historical_references.time_period: Classical Islamic period, 13th and 14th centuries AD
historical_references.context: Places of study and spiritual retreat

In the contemporary context, Ahdaaf is most commonly associated with sports training, education, and community building. On social media platforms such as Twitter, Instagram, and Facebook, the term is used to describe groups of individuals who support and motivate each other to excel in their chosen fields. For example, a group of young athletes might refer to themselves as 'Ahdaaf' on Twitter, using the hashtag #Ahdaaf to share training tips, inspirational quotes, and words of encouragement. Similarly, a group of students might use the term to describe their study group on Facebook, using the 'Ahdaaf' name to signify their commitment to learning and personal growth. Overall, the use of the term 'Ahdaaf' reflects a growing trend towards collective self-improvement and community support in the modern Islamic world.
